correctness.rationale: The Bernstein expansion is exact. Evaluating it at lambda=k*/n for an index attaining the maximum normalized elementary symmetric mean yields the reverse bound with factor b_{n,k*}. An exact adjacent-ratio calculation places the smallest b_{n,k} at the center. Sparse vectors with k central coordinates equal to L and the rest zero make the normalized optimized product converge uniformly to the central Bernstein basis polynomial, establishing sharpness. The p-value and Stirling corollaries then follow.
